inventory.visualPurpose: The two-group DRUG / ACTION / APPLICATIONS table (the section's sole printed element — the cholinomimetic drug grid: 4 direct agonists + 4 indirect agonists/anticholinesterases, plus the intro toxicity warning)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: ONE TWO-GROUP TEXT TABLE (PURE TEXT — ZERO rasters on pdf 261; pdfimages returns no rows; COPYRIGHTED, never reproduced as artwork). Column frame: DRUG / ACTION / APPLICATIONS. Group 1 'Direct agonists': Bethanechol — 'Activates bladder smooth muscle; resistant to AChE. Acts on muscarinic receptors; no nicotinic activity. "Bethany, call me to activate your bladder."' → 'Urinary retention.'; Carbachol — 'Carbon copy of acetylcholine (but resistant to AChE).' → 'Constricts pupil. Used for intraoperative miosis induction.'; Methacholine — 'Stimulates muscarinic receptors in airway when inhaled.' → 'Challenge test for diagnosis of asthma.'; Pilocarpine — 'Contracts ciliary muscle of eye (open-angle glaucoma), pupillary sphincter (closed-angle glaucoma); resistant to AChE, can cross blood-brain barrier. "You cry, drool, and sweat on your pilow."' → 'Potent stimulator of sweat, tears, and saliva / Open-angle and closed-angle glaucoma, xerostomia (Sjögren syndrome).' Group 2 'Indirect agonists (anticholinesterases)': Donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine — '↑ ACh.' → '1st line for Alzheimer disease (Dona Riva forgot the gala).'; Neostigmine — '↑ ACh. Neo = no blood-brain barrier penetration due to positive charge.' → 'Postoperative and neurogenic ileus and urinary retention, myasthenia gravis, reversal of neuromuscular junction blockade (postoperative).'; Pyridostigmine — '↑ ACh; ↑ muscle strength. Does not penetrate CNS. Pyridostigmine gets rid of myasthenia gravis.' → 'Myasthenia gravis (long acting). Used with glycopyrrolate or hyoscyamine to control pyridostigmine adverse effects.'; Physostigmine — '↑ ACh. Phreely (freely) crosses blood-brain barrier as not charged → CNS.' → 'Antidote for anticholinergic toxicity; physostigmine "phyxes" atropine overdose.' Intro warning above the table: 'Watch for exacerbation of COPD, asthma, and peptic ulcers in susceptible patients.' TEXT-LAYER ARTIFACTS: group labels print below their rows in the raw layer; '↑' glyphs carry a leading control char; Pilocarpine's raw layer prints 'bloodbrain' hyphen-less (Neostigmine/Physostigmine rows print 'blood-brain' with hyphen) — raw spellings pinned. Carried VERBATIM as the note's two table blocks and conveyed as ONE original KYP fork map (the direct-vs-indirect synapse fork, the eight drug cards, the charge grid, the toxicity strip, the reading-rule footer) — no artwork reproduced.

notes: Census (pdfimages + text layer): the section's printed visual set is ONE element — the TWO-GROUP DRUG/ACTION/APPLICATIONS TABLE, PURE TEXT (ZERO rasters on pdf 261 — pdfimages returns no rows; COPYRIGHTED, never reproduced as artwork).
